hens_rule_text: Up to 3 hens allowed with no minimum lot size, kept confined to the property by a fence or run.
permit_notes: No source found describing a separate chicken permit; regulation appears to be a straight zoning-code limit rather than a licensing scheme, but an official city permit page was not directly confirmed.
setback_notes: Code text (VMC 20.895.050) requires coops/shelters to sit in the rear yard and meet the same side and rear yard setbacks as the primary residence, with openings facing away from neighboring properties; it does not appear to set a flat foot distance from a neighbor's house, so no reliable number is given here.
coop_rules: Coop/shelter must be in the rear yard, meet the same side/rear setbacks as the main house, face away from neighboring properties, and animals must be confined or tethered so they cannot get onto neighboring property or damage neighboring landscaping/fences; must also comply with Ch. 20.935 VMC (Off-Site Impacts).
zoning_notes: Turkeys, peacocks and roosters are not permitted anywhere in the city; the rule is in VMC 20.895.050, Domestic Animals and Livestock, part of the general zoning code (Title 20).
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: 20.895.050 Domestic Animals and Livestock, Vancouver Municipal Code

research_notes: vancouver.municipal.codes returned a Cloudflare challenge page when fetched directly from this machine, so the section was not read verbatim; the 3-hen cap, no-rooster rule and rear-yard/setback language come from consistent search-result extracts of that same code section plus a 2025 local newspaper piece, but the exact setback distance from a neighbor's house could not be confirmed as a specific foot figure.
